Mateo / Laura — quick operational notes from SalesOps before Legal weighs in:

- SCCs: We can include the 2021 SCCs as an exhibit; operationally we treat those as a contractual reference and then implement via our processor controls. No blocker.
- Roles: PulseThera as Controller, Redwood as Processor is the expected mapping. If PulseThera wants any processor-subprocessor responsibilities to be elevated to controller obligations, flag those specifically.
- Subprocessor region limitation: This is the sticky bit. We do regional subprocessor routing for EU-restricted workloads via our EU private deployment and dedicated capacity. If PulseThera requires blanket limitation (no non-EU subprocessor access), we'd need either: (a) to commit their workload to EU-only dedicated pools (pricing uplift), or (b) provide a more technical routing SLA plus audits.

I've attached our internal draft 'Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.docx' with inline notes on the subprocessor clause and a suggested sentence to offer an operational alternative. If Legal signs off, I can prepare the redline to send to PulseThera.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

Team — reviewed PulseThera's addendum and Ben's draft. High-level: we can accept the SCCs exhibit and controller/processor mapping as-is. For the transfer-impact / subprocessor region restriction, propose the following approach:

1) Draft limited addendum language that commits to EU-only processing for covered workloads when the customer elects the "EU-dedicated" deployment option. I'll insert a conditional clause: "For workloads designated in the Order Form as EU-dedicated, Redwood will route processing to EU-only subprocessor and infrastructure providers subject to the routing list in Schedule A."

2) For customers that opt for standard hosted deployment but request limited-region covenants, we will provide an operational SLA and a quarterly attestation plus audit rights; pricing and capacity commitments to be captured in the order form.

3) I flagged PulseThera's proposed prohibition of certain cloud providers as too broad — will propose a carve that allows approved EU subprocessor vendors but excludes specifically disallowed regions.

Next steps: I'll produce a redline to their addendum and a short implementation note that outlines the EU-dedicated option and the uplift (ballpark 15% for dedicated pool).

Can one of you confirm whether PulseThera expects CMK (customer-managed keys) or just standard KMS? That affects the technical feasibility.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference
